title: Pressure-induced Structural Phase Transition, Metallization, and Superconductivity in layered metalloid dichalcogenide 1T-SiTe$_2$
authors: Ying-Jie Zhang, Heng Xu, Zhe-Ning Xiang, Zong-Hui Wu, Qing Li, Hai-Hu Wen
abstract: Layered transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have attracted considerable attention as promising platforms for exploring emergent physics and potential device applications. In contrast, metalloid-based dichalcogenide counterparts remain largely underexplored. Here, we report the pressure-induced structural phase transition, metallization, and superconductivity in the layered metalloid dichalcogenide 1T-SiTe$_2$. At ambient pressure, 1T-SiTe$_2$ crystallizes in a trigonal crystal structure (space group: $P\bar{3}m1$) and exhibits intrinsic semiconducting transport characteristics. Upon pressurization, in concomitant with the suppression of semiconducting behavior in resistance, superconductivity emerges at around 6.7 GPa. The superconducting transition temperature (T$_c$) rises continuously with increasing pressure and finally saturates at approximately 5.5 K for pressures above 30 GPa. During the compression, 1T-SiTe$_2$ experiences three structural phase transitions, and the phase transition pressures are highly consistent with the anomalous transport responses observed experimentally, indicating that the changes of transport behavior of 1T-SiTe$_2$ under pressure are structurally-driven. Our work extends TMD superconductors into the realm of metalloid systems and provides a new platform for exploring novel physics in quasi two-dimensional materials without transition-metal elements.
summary: This work reports on the discovery of superconductivity in 1T-SiTe2, a layered metalloid dichalcogenide. By applying high pressure, the material undergoes structural phase transitions that drive it from an ambient semiconducting state into a superconducting metallic phase. The findings establish a new platform for studying superconductivity outside traditional transition-metal systems.
main_problem: The study investigates how applying high pressure affects the structural phase transitions, metallization, and emergence of superconductivity in the layered metalloid dichalcogenide 1T-SiTe2.
main_result: Superconductivity emerges under pressure, with the critical temperature (Tc) increasing continuously up to a saturation value of approximately 5.5 K above 30 GPa. The superconducting behavior is strongly correlated with multiple structural phase transitions observed during compression.
method: The research employed high-pressure measurements using a Diamond Anvil Cell (DAC), combining electrical transport measurements (resistivity vs. temperature/field) with in-situ synchrotron X-ray Diffraction (XRD).
model_or_system: The physical system is the layered metalloid dichalcogenide 1T-SiTe2, which was characterized at ambient pressure and subjected to pressures up to 50 GPa. The study tracks structural changes through multiple identified phases (e.g., Phase I, II, III).
key_observables: Electrical resistivity ($ho$), superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$), magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$-$T$), and crystal structure parameters derived from high-pressure XRD.
important_parameters: Pressure range up to 50 GPa; $T_c$ saturation at $\sim 5.5 	ext{ K}$; ambient semiconducting behavior transitioning to metallic/superconducting states under pressure.
main_assumptions: The changes in transport properties are assumed to be structurally driven by the observed phase transitions, and the superconducting mechanism is suggested to potentially involve phonon mediation based on $H_{c2}$ analysis.
figures_summary: Figures detail ambient characterization (XRD, $ho$-$T$), high-pressure resistance curves showing superconductivity onset, in-situ XRD confirming three structural phases under pressure, and phase diagrams mapping $T_c$ vs. Pressure.
paper_structure: The paper follows a standard materials physics structure: initial ambient characterization of the semiconducting state; application of high pressure to induce metallization and observe superconductivity; detailed analysis linking specific structural transitions (via XRD) to anomalous transport responses ($ho$-$T$ curves).
why_interesting: While primarily experimental, the strong correlation between external tuning parameters (pressure) causing structural changes and emergent quantum phenomena (superconductivity) provides a model for understanding pressure-induced electronic state control relevant to condensed matter theory.
